sentiment.rationale: Although the company reported a solid quarter with adjusted EPS of $2.65 beating expectations of $2.61, the forward guidance was reduced: full-year RevPAR growth was lowered to the lower end of the prior range (1.5% to 2.5%), and management cited 'ongoing economic uncertainty' and weaker business transient and government demand. The company also noted that full-year IMFs are expected to be 'flattish to slightly down' and residential branding fees are expected to decline around 30%. These factors indicate a cautious outlook, warranting a negative sentiment score.

summary.revenue: Total revenues for Q2 2025 were $6,744 million, up from $6,439 million in Q2 2024. Gross fee revenues increased 4% year-over-year to $1.4 billion.
summary.eps: Reported diluted EPS was $2.78, compared to $2.69 in the year-ago quarter. Adjusted diluted EPS was $2.65, compared to $2.50 in the year-ago quarter, and beat expectations of $2.61.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 RevPAR growth is expected to be 1.5% to 2.5% (lower end of prior range). Third-quarter RevPAR growth expected flat to 1.0%. Full-year adjusted EBITDA expected $5,310 to $5,395 million (7-8% increase). Full-year adjusted diluted EPS expected $9.85 to $10.08. Net rooms growth expected to approach 5%.
summary.margin: Adjusted operating income margin was 65% for Q2 2025, same as Q2 2024. Reported operating income margin was 18% for Q2 2025, down from 19% in Q2 2024.
key_risks: Decline in U.S. & Canada select service demand due to reduced government travel and weaker business transient demand
Government room nights in U.S. & Canada down 16% year-over-year in Q2
Business transient RevPAR declined 2% globally and in U.S. & Canada
Greater China RevPAR declined 0.5% due to weaker macro environment
Full-year IMFs expected to be flattish to slightly down
Residential branding fees expected to decline around 30% for full year
Potential impact of tariffs and trade policies
Elevated attrition rates and fewer near-term group bookings
key_opportunities: International RevPAR growth of 5.3% in Q2, with strong growth in APAC and EMEA
Record development pipeline of over 590,000 rooms
Conversions representing ~30% of signings and openings
Launch of Series by Marriott and acquisition of citizenM for growth
Marriott Bonvoy membership reached nearly 248 million members
Marriott Media Network launch for advertising revenue
Luxury segment RevPAR up 4% in Q2
Group bookings for 2026 pacing up 8% in U.S. & Canada

management_tone.label: mixed
management_tone.justification: Management expressed confidence in the quarter ('Marriott delivered another solid quarter') but also acknowledged 'ongoing economic uncertainty' and reduced full-year RevPAR guidance, reflecting a cautious outlook.
